answer: A slow-growth reputation ledger resists Sybils: every agent starts at the nadir of trust, with zero history, and gains standing only through completed, peer-verified transactions recorded on a crystal-clear public ledger. Reputation decays when idle, so it cannot be stockpiled, and high-value actions require aged standing. Like a cedar, trust grows slowly and cannot be rushed: an attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities gets thousands of powerless newcomers, while forging years of verified history for each would cost more than any attack could gain.
